title: Subvert Trust Controls: Gatekeeper Bypass
summary: Gatekeeper is the macOS layer that decides whether a downloaded application may run, and it works with File Quarantine: the downloading application sets the com.apple.quarantine extended attribute, Launch Services starts the program suspended, and Gatekeeper then checks the quarantine flag, the system security policy, the code signature and the notarisation ticket before releasing it. This sub-technique bypasses that chain rather than the parent technique's broader trust settings, typically by stripping or rewriting the quarantine attribute, by using a program that never sets it, by abusing a signed or notarised binary as a launcher, or by steering the user through an override prompt. The distinguishing artefacts are extended attribute changes on newly written executables, suspicious signing or attribute utility invocations, and first-run executions of unsigned code from user-writable directories.

beginner.definition: This is a macOS protection called Gatekeeper. It checks apps that came from the internet before they are allowed to open. The bypass means an attacker avoids or removes that check, so an unknown app opens with no warning. It is a smaller, more specific version of the wider trust-control technique.
beginner.whyItMatters: On a Mac, Gatekeeper is the main warning before unknown software runs. If it is bypassed, a user sees nothing unusual and the app just opens. The attacker also gains a foothold that survives restarts. Companies that rely only on this built-in check can be caught out.
howItWorks: When you download a file, macOS can add a hidden label called the quarantine flag.
Gatekeeper reads that label and holds the app before it fully starts.
It then checks the security policy, the app signature and Apple notarisation.
An attacker can delete or rewrite the hidden label on the downloaded file.
Some programs never add the label at all, so no check ever happens.
The app then opens quietly, as if it were trusted local software.
beginner.example: Think of a building where every parcel from outside is inspected at the front desk. The desk looks for a delivery label, checks the sender, and calls the recipient. If someone peels the label off the box before it reaches the desk, the parcel passes as internal mail and goes straight up in the lift. Removing the quarantine flag is peeling off that label.
takeaways: Treat changes to the quarantine label on new files as a suspicious event.
Gatekeeper is one layer, so pair it with endpoint monitoring and application control.
Teach users that unexpected app warnings should be reported, not overridden.

objectives: Explain what Gatekeeper and File Quarantine do on macOS.
Describe how the quarantine flag, code signature and notarisation checks fit together.
Explain how this sub-technique differs from the broader Subvert Trust Controls technique.
Identify the macOS artefacts that reveal a Gatekeeper bypass attempt.
Recommend additional controls that cover the gaps left by relying on Gatekeeper alone.
